item.title: Classical solitons in anti-self-dual Yang-Mills theory
item.author: Tristan McLoughlin
item.description:
Tristan McLoughlin

Matched: tau function · hep-th · new

We study classical soliton solutions in split-signature anti-self-dual Yang-Mills theory. Using Zakharov's dressing method, we construct rational lump solitons, which are localised near two-dimensional surfaces, and wall solitons, which have codimension one. We further describe multi-phase solutions which have multiple walls meeting at trivalent junctions and form four-dimensional foam-like structures. Two-pole solutions describe soliton interactions and we find non-trivial colour-dressed phase shifts for wall interactions. We consider the four-dimensional analogue of Ward's lump scattering for the restricted kinematics of coincident poles and show that there are non-trivial interactions in the collinear limit. Finally, we show that the determinant of the soliton matrix provides a $\tau$-function which acts as a potential for gauge-invariant scalar quantities such as the Yang-Mills Lagrangian density.

item.title: Exact spectral integrability of a finite-channel random Schr\"odinger operator: from fermionization of the Dyson--Riccati gas to Kontsevich integral
item.author: Yan V. Fyodorov, Pierre Le Doussal
item.description:
Yan V. Fyodorov, Pierre Le Doussal

Matched: tau function · cond-mat.dis-nn, cond-mat.stat-mech, math-ph, math.MP · cross

We solve exactly, for arbitrary finite channel number $N$, the Riccati dynamics of a quasi-one-dimensional random matrix Schr\"odinger operator with Hermitian white-noise potential in the $\beta=2$ unitary symmetry class. The associated Dyson--Riccati eigenvalue gas admits an exact free-fermion representation at any sample length $L$, which in the limit $L\to \infty$ expresses the density of states and the total Lyapunov growth rate exactly through a single Airy Hankel $\tau$-function providing multichannel generalization of $N=1$ Halperin--Thouless formulas. The $\tau-$function further admits an outgoing-contour Kontsevich matrix Airy integral representation. Its saddle-point and double-scaling analyses give, in a unified way, the finite-channel density Lifshitz tail, and the large-$N$ spectral edge. In particular, for $N\gg 1$ the sharp $N=\infty$ edge is softened within an $N^{-4/5}$ spectral window, with its profile governed by the tritronqu\'ee solution of Painlev\'e I. We conjecture universality of this quasi-one-dimensional scaling edge profile for a broad class of $\beta=2$ random band matrices.

item.title: Painlev\'e II connection problem revisited
item.author: Nikolai Iorgov, Oleg Lisovyy, Noam Tamarin, Yurii Zhuravlov
item.description:
Nikolai Iorgov, Oleg Lisovyy, Noam Tamarin, Yurii Zhuravlov

Matched: tau function · nlin.SI, math-ph, math.MP · new

We study the inhomogeneous Painlev\'e II equation for generic monodromy data. Using Kapaev's asymptotic formulas, the parameters of Zak transform representations of the Painlev\'e II tau function on six special rays $\arg t=\frac{\pi p}{3}$ ($p=0,\ldots,5$) in the complex time plane are expressed in terms of Stokes parameters of the associated linear system. We then solve the connection problem for the tau function between these special rays, and provide analytical and numerical checks of our result.

item.title: Toda chain solves large BKP
item.author: Anton Zabrodin
item.description:
Anton Zabrodin

Matched: KdV · nlin.SI, math-ph, math.MP · new

We prove that any solution of the Toda chain hierarchy (the 1D reduction of the 2D Toda lattice) is a solution of the large BKP hierarchy. This is a difference analogue of Alexandrov's result that KdV solves (small) BKP.

item.title: On the hyperplane conjecture
item.author: Tsung-Ju Lee
item.description:
Tsung-Ju Lee

Matched: Gromov-Witten · math.AG, math.CV · new

We prove the hyperplane conjecture, proposed by Hosono, Lian, and Yau in arXiv:alg-geom/9511001 and its generalization to orbifolds. Consequently, this establishes the expected equivalence between the \(A\) model (genus-zero Gromov--Witten invariants with ambient insertions) of \(X\) and the \(B\) model (period integrals corresponding to vanishing cohomology) of \(X^{\vee}\) for Batyrev's mirror pair of Calabi--Yau hypersurfaces. As an application of our method, we also identify the residue of the Gauss--Manin connection and the cup product morphism on the \(A\)-side.

item.title: Realization of several related $(2+1)$-dimensional integrable systems via an anti-self-dual Yang--Mills reduction
item.author: Shangshuai Li, Ken-ichi Maruno, Da-jun Zhang
item.description:
Shangshuai Li, Ken-ichi Maruno, Da-jun Zhang

Matched: tau function · nlin.SI · new

We derive several integrable equations in $(2+1)$ dimensions from the anti-self-dual Yang--Mills (ASDYM) equations with gauge group $G=\mathrm{GL}(2,\mathbb C)$ by imposing a single one-dimensional constraint on the ASDYM matrices. The resulting systems include the $(2+1)$-dimensional nonlinear Schr\"odinger (NLS) equation, a $(2+1)$-dimensional generalized derivative NLS family encompassing the Gerdjikov--Ivanov, Chen--Lee--Liu, and Kaup--Newell equations, and the $(2+1)$-dimensional Heisenberg ferromagnetic (HF) equation. The $(1+1)$-dimensional Wadati--Konno--Ichikawa equation is also recovered through a reciprocal transformation of the HF equation. The nonlinear variables and the associated gauge transformations are expressed explicitly in terms of the entries of the ASDYM matrices. The same one-dimensional constraint is implemented in the Cauchy matrix framework, yielding explicit solutions of the reduced integrable equations. In this formulation, the ASD Yang--Mills Lagrangian density is expressed in terms of a $\tau$-function; for suitable exponential data, this $\tau$-function becomes a Grammian-type $\tau$-function of the Kadomtsev--Petviashvili equaton. The studies are extended to $\mathrm{GL}(M,\mathbb C)$ at the matrix level.

item.title: On the exact quantization of BCOV Theory on Calabi-Yau Manifolds
item.author: Si Li, Minghao Wang
item.description:
Si Li, Minghao Wang

Matched: Gromov-Witten · math-ph, hep-th, math.AG, math.DG, math.MP, math.QA · cross

We announce the solution of constructing perturbative quantum BCOV invariants on arbitrary Calabi-Yau manifolds. In this note, we outline the construction and present an explicit solution. The quantization includes all descendant fields and all loop orders, and expresses the quantum BCOV interaction by an explicit integration over the moduli space of marked Riemann surfaces. This canonical solution provides a mathematical construction of all higher genus BCOV invariants on compact Calabi-Yau manifolds, which are conjecturally equivalent to all higher genus Gromov-Witten invariants on the mirror.

item.title: Integral and higher-genus quantum McKay correspondence in type D
item.author: Andrea Brini, Jingxiang Ma
item.description:
Andrea Brini, Jingxiang Ma

Matched: Gromov-Witten · math.AG, hep-th · cross

We establish Iritani's integral form of the $\mathbb{C}^\times$-equivariant Crepant Transformation Conjecture (CTC) for the minimal resolution of the surface singularity $\mathbb{C}^2/\mathbb{BD}_{4n}$, where $\mathbb{BD}_{4n}$ is the binary dihedral group of order $4n$. We then use Givental's quantisation formalism to prove the all-genus full-descendent CTC in that case. As an application, we deduce the Bryan-Cadman-Young degree-zero form of the orbifold Gromov-Witten/Donaldson-Thomas correspondence for the Calabi-Yau 3-orbifold $[\mathbb{C}^2/\mathbb{BD}_{4n}] \times \mathbb{C}$.

item.title: Symmetries, Lax pair, and nilpotent Darboux transformation for the KdV-ghost system
item.author: A. Restuccia, J. Rosales-G\'omez, A. Sotomayor
item.description:
A. Restuccia, J. Rosales-G\'omez, A. Sotomayor

Matched: KdV · nlin.SI, math-ph, math.MP · new

We analyze the KdV--ghost system arising from the BRST formulation of BF-type topological field theory, its symmetries, Lax pair, spectral problem, zero-curvature formulation and Darboux formalism. The system is invariant under shifts of the ghost field, whose generator does not commute with the BRST symmetry of the KdV--ghost system. Their generators allow the introduction of a systematic procedure for generating new solutions from a given one, and the corresponding expressions in the Grassmann algebra are obtained explicitly. We introduce a Grassmann-valued Lax pair and prove an isospectral theorem relating the spectral problem of the spatial Lax operator for the KdV equation to that of its KdV--ghost extension. We also construct a triangular zero-curvature representation and show that the Grassmann-valued spatial Lax operator is related to the KdV spatial Lax operator by a nilpotent conjugation. The natural variable for a local Darboux formulation is the differentiated ghost $v=C_x$, for which the ghost equation coincides with the Fr\'echet linearization of the KdV flow. We then construct a nilpotent lift of the scalar KdV B\"acklund--Darboux transformation. Using Riccati variables and off-shell factorization identities for the KdV residue and its Fr\'echet derivative, we prove that the transformation closes on the local KdV--ghost system. Successive Darboux transformations yield a recursive ghost extension of the bosonic Darboux chain, with a new odd homogeneous contribution introduced at each step. For the solitonic examples, the resulting local ghost fields are naturally identified with tangent directions associated with the soliton phase parameters. The construction provides a Darboux-theoretic interpretation of the ghost sector while remaining distinct from the standard supersymmetric KdV hierarchies.

item.title: Gauss-Manin Connection in Disguise: Holomorphic Anomaly Equations and Higher Genus Real Gromov-Witten Invariants
item.author: Felipe Espreafico
item.description:
Felipe Espreafico

Matched: Gromov-Witten · math.AG, hep-th · cross

We construct an algebraic framework for the extended holomorphic anomaly equations following ideas of Alim, Movasati, Scheidegger and Yau. We choose the quintic threefold as our main model and use this framework to solve the equations and fix the ambiguity up to genus 5. We obtain predictions for real Gromov-Witten invariants, or, equivalently, real Gopakumar-Vafa invariants that are integers and agree with their complex counterparts modulo 2. In the end, we discuss how the framework could be extended and compute the same predictions for the bicubic up to genus 9.

item.title: Global Well-Posedness and Uniform Long-Time Control for a Class of Periodic NLS-Dysthe Equations
item.author: Andrea Belloni, Filippo Giuliani
item.description:
Andrea Belloni, Filippo Giuliani

Matched: KdV · math.AP, math-ph, math.MP · cross

We study a class of periodic NLS-Dysthe (NLS-Dy) equations, also referred to as higher-order nonlinear Schr\"odinger equations (HNLS), of the form $i\partial_t u+a\partial_x^2u+b|u|^2u+i\varepsilon(c\partial_x^3u+d|u|^2\partial_xu+eu^2\partial_x\overline{u})=0$ with $ x\in\mathbb T$, $a,b,c,d,e\in\mathbb R$, $abc eq0$, and $\varepsilon>0$. For $0<\varepsilon\ll1$, equations of this type arise as higher-order modulation models for some nonlinear dispersive PDEs, including the Klein-Gordon equation and the Serre-Green-Naghdi equation modeling the evolution of nonlinear shallow water waves. We prove local well-posedness in $H^s(\mathbb T)$ for $s>3/2$ for arbitrary admissible coefficients, and establish an $H^1$ continuation criterion for $s\ge2$. In the parameter regime $e eq0$, a lower-order conservation law provides uniform $H^1$ control and, together with the continuation criterion, yields global well-posedness for $s\ge2$. This result does not require the non-resonance condition appearing in Takaoka's periodic theory, while the condition $e eq0$ naturally arises in the modulation setting considered here. Finally, motivated by the long-time regime relevant for modulation, we establish uniform long-time control without imposing a smallness assumption on the initial datum. Using the conservation laws of cubic NLS and their invariance under the commuting complex mKdV flow, we obtain uniform $H^s$ bounds on time intervals of order $\varepsilon^{-1}$ for integer $s\ge2$. For non-integer real $s\ge2$, the maximal $H^s$ solution exists on the same time scale, while uniform control is obtained at a lower regularity, with a loss of less than one derivative.

item.title: Higher-order semi-rational solutions of the (2+1)-dimensional nonlocal multi-component Yajima--Oikawa system
item.author: Wenqiang Lu, Kelei Tian, Ying Xu, Ge Yi, Xiaoming Zhu
item.description:
Wenqiang Lu, Kelei Tian, Ying Xu, Ge Yi, Xiaoming Zhu

Matched: tau function · nlin.SI · new

Higher-order semi-rational solutions are constructed for the (2+1)-dimensional nonlocal multi-component Yajima-Oikawa system. This system is obtained from its local \(2M\)-component counterpart through a spatial-reflection reduction. Using Hirota's bilinear method and the Kadomtsev-Petviashvili hierarchy reduction, we derive a unified \(6\times6\) block Gram determinant. Its entries involve Schur polynomials and exponential functions. The complex-conjugation and spatial-reflection reductions are imposed through algebraic constraints on the spectral parameters and determinant blocks, with the former ensuring a real-valued denominator tau function. Separate spectral parameter sets are assigned to the rational, breather, and dark-soliton blocks. These solutions describe paired lumps or line rogue waves on breather, dark-soliton, or combined backgrounds. Pure rational, breather, and dark-soliton solutions follow by setting the appropriate block sizes to zero. Asymptotic analysis establishes the elastic interactions of the fundamental breather and dark-soliton pairs and determines their position and phase shifts.

item.title: Universality of $\mathsf{CohFT}$ of $\mathsf{Hilb}_n(S)$
item.author: Denis Nesterov, Hsian-Hua Tseng
item.description:
Denis Nesterov, Hsian-Hua Tseng

Matched: Gromov-Witten · math.AG · new

By virtue of their relation to Fulton--MacPherson compactifications, the cohomological field theory of Hilbert schemes of points on a surface, in extremal curve classes, is universally and effectively determined by the characteristic numbers of the surface and by the corresponding theory of Hilbert schemes of the affine plane. As a consequence, we compute the extremal genus 1 Gromov--Witten invariants of Hilbert schemes of all surfaces.

item.title: Two-Dimensional Torus Action on the Quadric Threefold and GW-DT-GV Correspondence
item.author: Kiryong Chung, Sanghyeon Lee
item.description:
Kiryong Chung, Sanghyeon Lee

Matched: Gromov-Witten · math.AG · new

We compute Gromov--Witten (GW) and Donaldson-Thomas (DT) invariants (including descendant invariants) for local CY $4$-folds over a smooth quadric threefold $Q$, up to degree $4$. We use the virtual localization formula with respect to a two-dimensional torus action to compute DT invariants. Combining these results with the computation of the J-function of the variety $Q$, we confirm the correspondence between DT and Gopakumar--Vafa invariants suggested by Cao--Maulik--Toda in genus zero. Based on these results, we predict a genus one BPS invariant on $Q$.

item.title: Irrational families of Fano weighted complete intersection fourfolds
item.author: Jiaji Cai, Andrew Harder, Sukjoo Lee
item.description:
Jiaji Cai, Andrew Harder, Sukjoo Lee

Matched: Gromov-Witten · math.AG, math.SG · cross

We study the irrationality of smooth Fano complete intersection fourfolds in weighted projective spaces, using an atom theoretic approach based solely on Gromov--Witten invariants. We prove symplectic irrationality, and hence irrationality for every smooth member, in a wide range of families for which irrationality was previously known only for very general members.

item.title: Open WDVV equations for non-commutative families of bounding cochains
item.author: Elad Kosloff
item.description:
Elad Kosloff

Matched: Gromov-Witten · math.SG, math.AG · new

We derive the noncommutative open WDVV equations for the open Gromov-Witten superpotential introduced in joint work of the author and Solomon, extending the Solomon-Tukachinsky equations to noncommutative differential graded algebras. The resulting recursive formulas facilitate the computation of open Gromov-Witten invariants with multiple boundary point constraints for even-dimensional Lagrangians. We apply the open WDVV equations to compute all open Gromov-Witten invariants for the real loci of even-dimensional complex quadrics of dimension greater than two. These computations show that open Gromov-Witten invariants with multiple boundary point constraints can be nontrivial in arbitrary dimensions. We also construct a character for a natural subalgebra of big quantum cohomology associated to a Lagrangian endowed with a point-like bounding cochain. The character is in the spirit of the Kodaira-Spencer map of Fukaya-Oh-Ohta-Ono. Applying the character construction to the even-dimensional quadric illustrates how point-like bounding cochains refine the information about closed quantum cohomology obtained from weak bounding cochains of Floer theory. Open Gromov-Witten invariants with three boundary point constraints determine the two extensions of the character from the subalgebra to big quantum cohomology.

item.author: Zhixuan Sheng, Jie Zhou

Zhixuan Sheng, Jie Zhou

item.title: Modular Properties of Generalised Gibbs Ensembles: The Deformed KdV Hierarchy
item.author: Faisal Karimi
item.description:
Faisal Karimi

Matched: KdV · hep-th, cond-mat.stat-mech, math-ph, math.MP · new

We construct a set of conserved charges which are deformations of quantum KdV charges. They are associated with the modular transformation of a GGE with the spin-$\sigma$ KdV charge inserted with chemical potential $\alpha_\sigma$. The charges are formal power series in the chemical potential, with coefficients given by local integrals of motion. We define local recursion relations and equivalent flow equations, prove commutativity to all orders, and establish uniqueness of the currents modulo total derivatives for a fixed generating series. We show that the eigenvalues of these deformed charges can be obtained from the thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz in two models. In the $c=1/2$ free fermion theory, the deformed charges reduce to explicit linear combinations of undeformed KdV charges, and their ground-state eigenvalues agree with the TBA expansion to all orders. In the Lee-Yang model, we find numerical agreement through cubic order in the spin-$5$ deformation for the first few charges evaluated on low-lying states.

item.title: The three- and four-loop equal-mass sunset integrals and local Calabi--Yau fourfolds and fivefolds
item.author: Hartmut Maennel, Pierre Vanhove
item.description:
Hartmut Maennel, Pierre Vanhove

Matched: Gromov-Witten · hep-th, math-ph, math.AG, math.MP · new

We determine the equal-mass two-dimensional three- and four-loop sunset Feynman integrals $I^{(3)}_\circleddash$ and $I^{(4)}_\circleddash$ at large Euclidean momentum in terms of the genus-zero Gromov--Witten theory of the local Calabi--Yau fourfold and fivefold $X_L=\operatorname{Tot}(K_{F_L})$, where $F_L\subset(\mathbb P^1)^{L+1}$, $L=3,4$, is a smooth hypersurface of multidegree $(1,\ldots,1)$. At two loops the sunset integral is governed by the prepotential of a local Calabi--Yau threefold. For $L\geq3$ the moduli spaces of unmarked stable maps have positive virtual dimension and there is no prepotential, therefore the Feynman integral is governed instead by the one-point potential $\mathcal F_{\gamma_L}$ with insertion $\gamma_L=H^{L-1}/(L-1)!$, by its gravitational descendants, and by $\zeta(3)$ boundary terms coming from the Gamma class. At both loop orders the coefficient of $R^{L-1}$ in the Frobenius expansion in the mirror coordinate $R$ is $-\theta_Q\mathcal F_{\gamma_L}$ with the Novikov variable $Q=\exp(R)$. At three loops the whole Feynman integral is an explicit expression in $\mathcal F_{\gamma_3}$ alone, because genus-zero recursion determines all descendant series from it; at four loops two diagonal series suffice, and the $\zeta(3)$ term is itself corrected by $\theta_Q\mathcal F_{\gamma_4}$. At three loops we also derive the analytic normalization independently, from the Picard--Fuchs equation and the polar part of a Mellin transform, prove integrality of the multiple-cover transforms for arbitrary integral insertions together with an explicit quantum-$K$ formula, and compute the exact period connection polynomials. Finally we give endpoint values along the Euclidean axis, bounds on the Taylor radii in the Novikov variable $Q$, a computer-assisted proof of the four-loop endpoint nonanalyticity, and a comparison of the normalizations at two, three and four loops.

item.title: Equal-mass sunset integrals and genus-zero local Gromov--Witten theory of Calabi--Yau $n$-folds
item.author: Hartmut Maennel, Pierre Vanhove
item.description:
Hartmut Maennel, Pierre Vanhove

Matched: Gromov-Witten · math.AG, hep-th, math-ph, math.MP · cross

We prove an exact identity, as convergent logarithmic germs at large Euclidean momentum, between the equal-mass two-dimensional $(n-1)$-loop sunset Feynman integral, with $n\geq4$, and the genus-zero one-point descendant invariants of the local Calabi--Yau $n$-fold $X_n=\operatorname{Tot}(K_{F_n})$, where $F_n\subset(\mathbb P^1)^{n}$ is a smooth $(1,\ldots,1)$ hypersurface. Writing $s$ for the momentum variable and $y=-1/s$, the identity reads $$ I^{(n-1)}_{\circleddash}(s)=(-1)^{n-1}yA\,\Bigl[nR^{n-1}-\theta_Q{\mathcal D}_0^\Delta\,R^{n-2} +\sum_{j=0}^{n-3}c_jR^j\Bigr], $$ where $R=\log y+O(y)$ is the local mirror coordinate, $A=\theta_yR$, $Q=e^R$, ${\mathcal D}_0^\Delta(Q)$ is the primary one-point potential, and each $c_j$ is an explicit linear combination of $1$, the descendant series ${\mathcal D}_a^\Delta(Q)$ and their derivatives $\theta_Q{\mathcal D}_a^\Delta$, $0\leq a\leq n-2$, with coefficients in the odd-zeta values $\mathbb Q[\zeta(3),\zeta(5),\ldots]$ coming from the Gamma class. The descendant series are given explicitly by the ambient hypergeometric series and the inverse mirror map. We also prove global univalence of the principal mirror map, with explicit upper and lower bounds on the $Q$-Taylor radii, extract the full primary evaluation divisor and its integral cover transform, and reduce the ambient endpoint constants to a finite universal Gamma-class part and $\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor$ real parameters.

item.title: From wall structures to closed mirror symmetry. The case of $K_{\mathbb{P}^2}$: Renormalized periods over the positive real locus, closed Gromov-Witten invariants from wall functions, and tropical enumeration
item.author: Michel van Garrel, Bernd Siebert
item.description:
Michel van Garrel, Bernd Siebert

Matched: Gromov-Witten · math.AG · new

We recover closed Gromov-Witten invariants and renormalized mirror periods for $K_{\mathbb{P}^2}$ by the same operation on a wall function. This gives a direct passage from the Gross-Siebert construction of intrinsic mirror pairs to classical enumerative mirror symmetry. The link is a polynomiality theorem for punctured invariants. Assuming the expected identification with the normalized slab function, we also obtain a finite tree sum for closed Gromov-Witten invariants in terms of types of plane tropical curves. The mechanism is expected to extend to more general Calabi-Yau mirror pairs.

item.title: On leading Gopakumar--Vafa invariants of local $\mathbb{P}^2$ and leading Betti numbers of moduli spaces of one-dimensional sheaves on $\mathbb{P}^2$
item.author: Zhiyuan Wang, Chenglang Yang
item.description:
Zhiyuan Wang, Chenglang Yang

Matched: Gromov-Witten · math.AG, math-ph, math.MP, math.SG · cross

In this paper we use the topological vertex formalism to derive a structural formula for the leading terms of the generating series of Gromov--Witten invariants of local $\mathbb P^2$. Then we give two applications of this formula. First we use this result to derive an explicit formula for the leading terms of the transformed Gopakumar--Vafa invariants of local $\mathbb P^2$. This is an extension of a formula of Guo--Zhou \cite{gz} from degree $2d-5$ to $3d-1$, and shares some similar features with the famous G\"ottsche--Yau--Zaslow formula. And as the second application, we prove Guo--Wu--Moreira's Conjecture \cite{gw} about the leading Betti numbers of the moduli space of one-dimensional Gieseker semistable sheaves on $\mathbb P^2$.

item.title: The Riemann theta function near soliton limit
item.author: Yuji Kodama
item.description:
Yuji Kodama

Matched: KdV · nlin.SI, math-ph, math.AG, math.MP · new

It has been known that (the square of) Jacobi elliptic function can be expressed by an infinite sum of single solitons of $\sech^2$ shape. In this paper, we show that there exists a similar structure for higher genus cases. It turns out that this is just a consequence of the quasi-periodicity of the Riemann $\theta$-function. More precisely, we show that the second derivative of $\log \theta$ with the \emph{real} Riemann $\theta$-function of genus $g$ near soliton limit can be well approximated by the \emph{sum} of \emph{real} and \emph{regular} $g$-soliton solutions of Hirota-type in $g$-dimensional real space $\R^g$. This leads to a tessellation of $\R^g$, whose tile is an oblique prism divided into $2^g$ sections by hyper-planes of dominant exponents in the theta function. We apply the results to study quasi-periodic solutions to the KdV and KP equations. We construct the quasi-periodic solutions using the Schottky group, which uniformizes the corresponding Riemann surfaces. We also discuss solitons on quasi-periodic background by pinching some of the homological cycles

item.title: Generalized eigenstate thermalization beyond leading order in 2D large c CFTs
item.author: Ziyuan Wang, Jiaju Zhang
item.description:
Ziyuan Wang, Jiaju Zhang

Matched: KdV, Korteweg-de Vries · hep-th · new

We develop a Fock-space formulation that reduces expectation values of vacuum-family quasi-primaries in qKdV eigenstates of arbitrary highest-weight conformal families to a free-bosonic problem, and employ it to test the generalized eigenstate thermalization hypothesis (GETH), in 2D conformal field theories with large central charge $c$. We demonstrate that the first two quantum Korteweg--de Vries (qKdV) charges $Q_1$ and $Q_3$ lift all degeneracies except along at most countably many curves in the $(c,\Delta)$ plane, where $\Delta$ is the highest weight of the conformal family, so that the full-qKdV simultaneous eigenstates are unambiguously determined by $Q_1$ and $Q_3$. Based on this, a near-complete toolkit for testing in the vacuum conformal family or falsifying the general form of GETH, i.e. equating qKdV eigenstates and thermal states of the generalized Gibbs ensemble in the sense of expectations of local observables, is provided in this paper, through the infinite tower of qKdV charges. A stronger form of the GETH, namely that all expectations of local observables of a definite level should be expressible of qKdV charges but not contain microscopic eigenstate information, is directly falsified at subleading order in the large-$c$ expansion. At levels 6 and 8 in the vacuum family, expectation values of quasi-primaries in simultaneous eigenstates of the qKdV charges are not fixed by first finitely many qKdV charges, and microscopic information of the eigenstate is required.

item.title: Completed cycle transfer and the conifold gap for (P^2, E)
item.author: Xiaobin Li
item.description:
Xiaobin Li

Matched: Gromov-Witten · math.AG · new

Conifold boundary conditions constrain higher genus topological string free energies, but the cancellation of subleading poles is not implied by their leading singular behavior. We prove a regularity theorem for connected elliptic completed cycle traces and use it to establish the Nekrasov-Shatashvili conifold gap for the maximal contact relative Gromov-Witten theory of the projective plane with a smooth cubic boundary and a top Hodge class insertion. The higher genus local/relative correspondence expresses the ordinary potential in terms of the relative potential and differentiated lower genus contributions. We identify its conifold polarized correction with an elliptic trace. A central difference identity resums each non-vacuum partition weight into a content product multiplied by a regular exponential. For arbitrary regular parts of the input potentials and any nome with a simple zero, the normalized non-vacuum connected contribution is divisible by the conifold coordinate and by the square of the coupling. The entire polar part and finite part are consequently determined by the vacuum constants. A triangular induction transfers the known ordinary local projective plane gap to the relative theory. We also obtain finite part identities, finite formulas for regular Taylor coefficients, and reconstruction of the holomorphic ambiguities. The argument is formal in the coupling and gives holomorphic remainders at every fixed genus.

item.title: Conifold factorization in topological recursion and Gromov--Witten theory
item.author: Juping Chen, Linji Chen, Bohan Fang, Zhengyu Zong
item.description:
Juping Chen, Linji Chen, Bohan Fang, Zhengyu Zong

Matched: Gromov-Witten · math.AG, math-ph, math.MP · cross

We prove a factorization theorem for ordinary topological recursion near a regular nodal degeneration of a spectral curve, allowing logarithmic spectral coordinates. The partition function for closed genera $g\ge2$ factors into the partition function of the normalization, a universal Gaussian vacuum, and the exponential of a connected graph sum. This graph sum has strictly positive order in the vanishing period, and thus the factorization recovers the conifold gap, identifies the term of degree zero in the vanishing period with the free energy of the normalization, and gives finite graph formulas for the coefficients of positive powers of the period. At fixed genus, the regular series converges jointly in the period and the parameters along the nodal locus. The Gaussian neck tensors can be expressed in terms of relative Gromov--Witten invariants of a parametrized $\mathbb P^1$. As examples, we use remodeling to obtain Gromov--Witten factorizations for local $\mathbb P^2$ and local $\mathbb F_0$ in the conifold frame, with backgrounds $\mathbb C^3$ and the resolved conifold, respectively. The analogous local $\mathbb F_1$ factorization has background $\mathcal O(1)\oplus\mathcal O(-3)$ over $\mathbb P^1$.

item.title: Quantum hierarchies of the ILW and BO equations and the DR cycles on the moduli spaces of curves
item.author: Alexandr Buryak, Abner Hernandez Rodriguez
item.description:
Alexandr Buryak, Abner Hernandez Rodriguez

Matched: Korteweg-de Vries · math-ph, math.AG, math.MP, nlin.SI · cross

In an earlier paper of P. Rossi and the first author, a construction of a wide class of quantum hierarchies was presented, with the input data given by an arbitrary cohomological field theory. A crucial role in the construction is played by the double ramification (DR) cycles on the moduli spaces of stable curves. As a special case, one gets a quantization of the hierarchy of the Intermediate Long Wave (ILW) equation. The ILW equation has two famous limits: the Korteweg--de Vries equation and the Benjamin--Ono (BO) equation, and for the latter one a quantum hierarchy was constructed by Nazarov and Sklyanin. In our paper, we propose a conjecture describing a relation between a limit of the quantum ILW hierarchy and the Nazarov--Sklyanin hierarchy and present various checks to support it.

item.title: Intrinsic mirror symmetry for orbifold cubic surfaces and the $A_1$ spherical DAHA
item.author: Pierrick Bousseau, Sayan Chattopadhyay
item.description:
Pierrick Bousseau, Sayan Chattopadhyay

Matched: Gromov-Witten · math.AG, hep-th, math.GT · cross

We determine the intrinsic mirror of an orbifold cubic surface with three nodes and interpret the resulting geometry through mirror symmetry between the $PGL(2,\mathbb{C})$ and $SL(2,\mathbb{C})$ character varieties of the once-punctured torus. We further construct a quantization of the mirror using higher genus Gromov-Witten theory and show that it recovers the $A_1$ spherical double affine Hecke algebra.

item.title: Structure of higher-genus open-closed Gromov--Witten theory of $\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{1}}(p-1)\oplus\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{1}}(-p-1)$
item.author: Shuai Guo, Jingyi Xu, Qingsheng Zhang
item.description:
Shuai Guo, Jingyi Xu, Qingsheng Zhang

Matched: Gromov-Witten · math.AG, math-ph, math.MP · cross

We study the closed and open Gromov--Witten potentials of the toric Calabi--Yau threefold $$ X_p=\operatorname{Tot}\bigl(\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{1}}(p-1)\oplus\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{1}}(-p-1)\bigr),\qquad p\geq 2. $$ We prove closed and open mirror symmetry under a nonvanishing condition on the torus weights, relating these potentials to topological recursion on the mirror curves. We establish polynomial structures for both the higher-genus closed potentials and the stable open potentials. We also establish double-scaling limits for topological recursion on the mirror curves. In particular, our results for the closed potentials prove the higher-genus ansatz and the double-scaling conjecture of Caporaso--Griguolo--Mari\~no--Pasquetti--Seminara.

item.title: Fredholm determinant solutions to the modified KP hierarchy and 2D Toda lattice: isospectral and non-isospectral reductions
item.author: Dan Dai, Han-Han Sheng
item.description:
Dan Dai, Han-Han Sheng

Matched: KdV, Korteweg-de Vries · nlin.SI, math-ph, math.MP · new

We study Fredholm determinant solutions to the first two positive and the first negative members of the modified Kadomtsev-Petviashvili (mKP) hierarchy, together with the bilinear two-dimensional Toda lattice (2DTL) equation. By applying isospectral reductions, we explicitly construct Fredholm determinant solutions for the modified Korteweg-de Vries (mKdV), the modified Camassa-Holm, and the focusing nonlinear Schr\"odinger equations. Furthermore, we demonstrate that in the non-isospectral case, the reduction from the mKP and 2DTL equations to the non-isospectral negative KdV equation yields solutions characterized by the deformed Bessel determinant.

item.title: Revisiting three-dimensional GLSMs and K-theoretic I-functions
item.author: Taro Kimura, Yinda Li, Xiaohan Yan
item.description:
Taro Kimura, Yinda Li, Xiaohan Yan

Matched: Gromov-Witten · hep-th, math.AG · new

We revisit the correspondence between three-dimensional gauged linear sigma models and K-theoretic Gromov-Witten theory. We show that the K-theoretic Hori-Vafa formula for the grassmannian arises from the three-dimensional gauge theory upon including an appropriate anomaly-cancellation factor. Furthermore, we derive K-theoretic I-functions for isotropic grassmannians by incorporating symmetric and anti-symmetric tensor representation fields together with suitable boundary conditions.

item.title: Resolvent reconstruction of minimal strings beyond KdV
item.author: Wasif Ahmed, Joydeep Naskar
item.description:
Wasif Ahmed, Joydeep Naskar

Matched: KdV · hep-th · new

Minimal strings offer two ways to study quantum surfaces: through a spectral curve or through a differential equation. We ask how much of the quantum equation can be recovered once the classical curve and its motion with the background are known. Our starting point is the resolvent of a scalar differential operator. We require its one-boundary integral to have poles only at branch points, with the resulting differential regular at infinity. These conditions give a finite reconstruction procedure at each genus. When the branch points are simple and their energy values move, we prove that the quantum corrections are unique whenever the procedure is consistent. A specified string equation provides a solution if its trace primitive satisfies the same analytic conditions. The scalar construction also leads to amplitudes with several boundaries. We introduce the method through pure gravity and Ising, then explore higher-order, dual and nonunitary models. Higher-Airy examples connect the calculation to $r$-spin theory on a degenerate locus that requires a separate treatment of the inverse problem.
